 Right Arrow Airlines Popular airline hits customers with steep fee hike for first time in 8 years
 Some travelers won't stomach the jump in airline credit card fees even with added perks, experts say
 By
 Kelly McGreal Fox News 
 Published
 October 29, 2026 8:00am EDT Comments

 close Video Airline credit card shake-up raises questions about whether perks are worth it 
 The Points Guy editor Nick Ewen breaks down American Airlines' upcoming credit card changes, including higher annual fees and additional benefits.
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 The era of the standard $99 airline credit card may be fading as American Airlines becomes the latest major carrier to adjust its price tag.
 Beginning Jan. 24, 2027, the annual fee for both the Citi/AAdvantage Platinum Select MasterCard and the Citi/AAdvantage Business MasterCard will jump from $99 to $150, according to a company press release.
 The adjustment marks the first price hike for the popular Platinum Select consumer card since 2018, signaling a shift in the travel rewards landscape.
 MAJOR AIRLINE DITCHES SNACKS DURING SHORT FLIGHTS AS ‘ZERO SERVICE’ SPARKS DEBATE 
 To soften the blow of a nearly 52% fee increase, American Airlines, Citi and MasterCard are adding several new travel and lifestyle perks.
 Whether those additions make up for the $51 increase will depend largely on how travelers use the card, Nick Ewen, editor-in-chief of The Points Guy, told Fox News Digital. 
 "You have to look at the real dollar value based on your own travel habits," said Ewen, who is based in Florida. 
 American Airlines customers with select Citi/AAdvantage credit cards will see their annual fees rise from $99 to $150 beginning Jan. 24, 2027. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images) 
 Cardholders will gain additional ways to earn AAdvantage miles on everyday spending, along with up to $120 toward Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees every four years, American Airlines confirmed.
 Additionally, a new $100 annual statement credit for in-flight purchases will replace the previous 25% food and beverage discount. 
 This makes the card significantly more rewarding for travelers, as the credit can be applied toward broad in-flight expenses, including Wi-Fi, which was explicitly excluded under the old discount system.
 "You may not be able to stomach that additional increased annual fee."
 For someone who regularly spends money aboard American flights or already pays for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck, Ewen said the new credits could help offset the higher annual fee.
 "If the answer is yes, you're definitely going to come out ahead," he said of travelers who typically spend up to $100 on in-flight purchases each year.
 PASSENGER JET BOUND FOR US PLUNGES 27,000 FEET BEFORE CIRCLING FOR HOURS 
 The changes may not be for everyone, however.
 "If you're only flying American once a year, you may not be able to stomach that additional increased annual fee," he said.
 Some travelers are wondering whether the added benefits will justify the higher annual fees. (iStock) 
 The changes also include adjustments to how cardholders can rack up rewards on everyday purchases, according to the press release. 
 The personal Platinum Select card will offer three miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and Cars bookings and two miles per dollar on gas and EV charging , select streaming services, and eligible Rides and Rails purchases.
 CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER 
 Existing perks — including preferred boarding, no foreign transaction fees and a free first checked bag on domestic American itineraries for the cardholder and up to four companions — will remain intact.
 Ewen said the higher fee follows a broader shift among airline rewards cards. 
 "American is far from the first airline that we've seen this increase in their annual fees," he said, pointing to similar changes from Delta, Southwest and United.
 American Airlines' credit card changes come amid a broader industry trend of airline rewards cards moving toward annual fees of approximately $150. (Li Rui/Xinhua via Getty Images) 
 Entry-level airline cards that once hovered around $100 annually are increasingly moving closer to $150, Ewen said.
 "This is definitely the norm, although it's not universal across the board," he added.
 CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES 
 The move by American Airlines aligns with a broader trend sweeping the credit card sector. 
 Over the past few years, the travel rewards market has seen steady fee inflation as issuers pack mid-tier and premium cards with statement credits and subscription services.
 The move by American Airlines aligns with a broader trend sweeping the credit card sector.
 Financial institutions are betting consumers will accept higher upfront costs in exchange for tangible, use-it-or-lose-it perks, transforming traditional flight-focused credit cards into broader lifestyle products, according to reports. 
 The changes drew mixed reactions from cardholders online.
 TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ 
 "Call me crazy, but none of this is an upgrade," one Reddit user commented.
 Another questioned the value of the new in-flight credit . 
 To soften the blow of a 52% fee increase, American Airlines, Citi and MasterCard are adding several new travel and lifestyle perks. (Mark Felix/Bloomberg via Getty Images) 
 "These inflight credit[s] [are] annoying," the person wrote. "They don't even stock them except for longer flights."
 Others were more receptive to the new benefits, with one commenter pointing to the Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit as a reason the higher fee could be worthwhile.

 "This has become more of a respectable airline card in my opinion now with this refresh," one user wrote.
